why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 test only what their expect lines say. Check 1 covers the export, left padding with an explicit fill and the default space fill. Check 2 covers input that is exactly width long or longer coming back unchanged. Check 4 needs exit 0 with no failing tests. The advisories are kept out of every PASS/FAIL condition. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS needs "prints ALL DOCUMENTED", and the regex `'^#{1,6}\\s+\`?'+k+'\\b'` only matches a heading whose first word is the exact, case-sensitive function name. The words "a section for every function index.js exports" don't require that heading format. A real section such as "## Padding with padLeft" or "## `strutil.padLeft`" would print MISSING and FAIL. That is a heading-format rule stricter than the expect line, and it sits inside a PASS/FAIL condition instead of under Advisory.
